does: Fries thinly sliced onions in a generous amount of fat until their water has gone and they turn deep brown and crisp, then lifts them out to drain. They are crushed into a marinade, layered into rice, scattered on top, or stirred into a gravy.

intro.what: This method fries thin onions deep brown and drains them so they crisp as they cool.
intro.why: It teaches you to anticipate continued darkening and lift onions out before the final colour goes too far.

how: Slice the onions thin and even, so that they brown together. Spread them out to dry a little if they are wet.
Heat plenty of fat in a wide pan until a slice sizzles at once, then add the onions in a loose layer.
Stir often at a steady medium heat. They go limp, then pale gold, then amber.
Lower the heat as the colour deepens. The last stage takes only moments, so stay at the pan.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon the moment they are deep brown, and spread them on paper to drain. They crisp as they cool.

cues.text: The slices pass from limp and pale to amber and then deep brown, with the edges darkest.
The sizzle is loud while the onions are wet and fades to a quiet crackle as the water goes.
A slice lifted out and left to cool snaps between the fingers.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding the pan, so that the onions steam and stay limp and pale.
mistakes.fix: Fry in a wide pan, in a thin layer, or in batches.

mistakes.mistake: Walking away at the end, when the onions turn from brown to bitter black in moments.
mistakes.fix: Lift them out while they are a shade lighter than wanted. They go on darkening in the fat they carry.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving them in the hot fat to cool, so that they go soft and greasy.
mistakes.fix: Lift them out and spread them on paper at once.

quiz.question: Why lift the onions out of the fat to cool?
choices: So they stop developing any crispness.
So they retain a coating of pooled fat.
So they drain and crisp instead of becoming soft and greasy.
quiz.because: Onions left cooling in hot fat can become soft and greasy; draining lets them crisp.

quiz.question: How should you adjust heat as their colour deepens?
choices: Lower it and stay beside the pan.
Raise it to speed the final browning.
Keep it high and leave them unattended.
quiz.because: The final darkening happens quickly, so lower heat and close attention matter.

quiz.question: What happens to the sound as water leaves the onions?
choices: A quiet start grows into a constant roar.
A loud sizzle fades to a quiet crackle.
quiz.because: Less water remains as frying progresses, and the loud sizzle fades.

quiz.question: The onions kept darkening into bitterness after lifting. What would you change for the next batch?
choices: Wait for darker edges before draining.
Leave them in the fat until cool.
Lift them a shade lighter because they continue darkening.
quiz.because: The fat carried on the onions continues darkening them after lifting, so anticipate that change.

comes_after.why: Slices of an even width brown together, so the cook has to be able to slice onions evenly first.

variant_of.differs: Caramelising keeps the onions soft and sticky, in little fat and over a low heat. Here the slices swim in a generous amount of fat at a steady medium heat until they dry out, turn deep brown and crisp, and are lifted out and drained, to be used as a topping, a layer or a flavouring.
